description: Fig. 20 is a composite two-row figure comparing experiment (a) with 3D cellular-automaton simulation (b) for a transient strain-rate decrease from 0.1 s⁻¹ to 0.01 s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain and 950 °C. Row (a) is three column-pairs of EBSD maps, each carrying a 100 μm scale bar: the upper image of each pair is a colour-coded IPF map and the lower one a GOS map whose blue/green/yellow fields encode DRX fractions. Column 1 (950°C_0.1s⁻¹, constant-rate reference) is labelled "0.4 strain: 81.50±6.32μm" with "DRX fraction: 38.9%"; column 2 (950°C_0.1s⁻¹_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4)) is "0.5 strain: 52.92±3.35μm" with "DRX fraction: 95.2%"; column 3 (same label) is "0.9 strain: 50.71±3.29μm" with "DRX fraction: 97.7%". Row (b) shows three 3D CA cubes (100 μm scale bars, XYZ axes) labelled 42.9% (0.4 strain: 82.68μm), 99.1% (0.5 strain: 50.78μm) and 99.8% (0.9 strain: 52.58μm), with a legend "White grains: matrix, Green grains: first stage (950°C_0.1s⁻¹), Red grains: second stage (950°C_0.01s⁻¹)". Experiment and simulation agree: DRX fraction jumps from ~39-43% to >95-99% between 0.4 and 0.5 strain, then the average grain size drops slightly to ~0.9 strain.

observations.observation: The upper-left EBSD IPF map is printed '950°C_0.1s⁻¹' and '0.4 strain: 81.50±6.32μm' with a 100 μm scale bar, and the paired GOS map gives 'DRX fraction: 38.9%' or the DRX-fraction reference state.

The middle and right (a) columns are both labelled '950°C_0.1s⁻¹_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4)' and report '0.5 strain: 52.92±3.35μm / DRX fraction: 95.2%' and '0.9 strain: 50.71±3.29μm / DRX fraction: 97.7%' respectively.
In the GOS maps the recrystallized area expands from a limited yellow-green central region at 0.4 strain to an almost fully uniform field at 0.5 and 0.9 strain.
The three CA cubes in (b) are labelled 42.9%, 99.1% and 99.8% at 0.4 strain (82.68μm), 0.5 strain (50.78μm) and 0.9 strain (52.58μm), each with 100 μm scale bars.
The (b) legend defines 'White grains: matrix', 'Green grains: first stage(950°C_0.1s⁻¹)' and 'Red grains: second stage(950°C_0.01s⁻¹)'.
In (b), the white matrix fraction disappears from the 0.4-strain cube to the 0.5-strain cube, where red second-stage grains first appear and then dominate the 0.9-strain cube.

Both experiment (a) and simulation (b) show a sharp DRX jump of roughly 50-60 percentage points over the 0.4 → 0.5 strain interval, and a small decrease in average grain size thereafter (81.50→50.71 μm experimental; 82.68→52.58 μm simulated).

The figure presents experimental and simulated microstructure evolution resulting from transiently decreasing strain rates from 0.1 s⁻¹ to 0.01 s⁻¹ at 0.4 strain and 950 °C, with (a) IPF and GOS maps and (b) simulation results.

After the strain rate was suddenly decreased at 0.4 strain, the incomplete-recrystallization microstructure rapidly transitioned into a nearly full recrystallization state within a strain interval of 0.1.

The citing text states that the microstructure at 0.5 strain in Fig. 20a was almost identical to that at a constant strain rate of 0.01 s⁻¹ and 0.9 strain in Fig. 19a, and that the final AGS underwent a little drop.

The citing text attributes to (b) that a sudden strain-rate decrease made DRX grains formed during the first stage (950 °C and 0.1 s⁻¹) grow rapidly, refining the matrix almost completely by 0.5 strain.

The caption and the citing text both present (b) as CA-model simulation output matching the experimental DRX evolution measured in (a); no IPF colour-orientation triangle or colour key is printed anywhere in the figure.

subfigures.description: IPF map titled '950°C_0.1s⁻¹' with printed '0.4 strain: 81.50±6.32μm' and a 100 μm scale bar; coarsely banded, strongly colour-contrasted grains typical of incomplete recrystallization.
GOS map with printed 'DRX fraction: 38.9%' and 100 μm scale bar; predominantly blue (unrecrystallized matrix) with a large yellow-green recrystallized region in the centre.
IPF map titled '950°C_0.1s⁻¹_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4)' with '0.5 strain: 52.92±3.35μm' and 100 μm scale bar; notably finer, equiaxed grains than the left column.
GOS map with 'DRX fraction: 95.2%' and 100 μm scale bar; almost entirely blue with small green/red islands, i.e. nearly full recrystallization.
IPF map titled '950°C_0.1s⁻¹_0.01s⁻¹(ε₁=0.4)' with '0.9 strain: 50.71±3.29μm' and 100 μm scale bar; grain structure similar to the 0.5 strain state with slight coarsening of individual grains.
GOS map with 'DRX fraction: 97.7%' and 100 μm scale bar; essentially uniform blue field with a single small green recrystallized patch.
3D CA simulation cube labelled '42.9%' with '0.4 strain: 82.68μm' and a 100 μm scale bar; white matrix grains forming a continuous skeleton with scattered green first-stage DRX grains.
3D CA simulation cube labelled '99.1%' with '0.5 strain: 50.78μm' and a 100 μm scale bar; grain structure dominated by green first-stage grains with numerous red second-stage grains.
3D CA simulation cube labelled '99.8%' with '0.9 strain: 52.58μm' and a 100 μm scale bar; surface almost entirely red (second-stage DRX) with green grains remaining.
Legend text 'White grains: matrix Green grains: first stage(950°C_0.1s⁻¹) Red grains: second stage(950°C_0.01s⁻¹)' and a black XYZ reference triad marking the 3D sample coordinates.

unreadable_items: No IPF colour-orientation legend/triangle is printed, so the crystallographic meaning of the IPF map colours cannot be read
No axis or colour scale is given for the GOS maps (only DRX fraction percentages)
The small white 100 μm scale bars printed on the faces of the (b) cubes are only partially readable at the supplied resolution
